metadata.Syllabus Name: Introduction to Generative AI_Nhập môn TTNT tạo sinh
metadata.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
metadata.Description: The course gives students a working understanding of how modern generative AI models work and how to use them well. The course covers foundations and intuition of large language models, diffusion and multimodal models; prompt engineering and evaluation; retrieval-augmented generation (RAG); building applications with model APIs; agents and tool use; customization (prompting, RAG, fine-tuning); failure modes and evaluation; and ethics, safety, and governance. Mathematical internals are deferred to the Deep Learning course; this course stays at the level of intuition while building real, hands-on skill.
metadata.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Students are responsible for completing all exercises, labs, and the term project given by the instructor, in class or at home, and submitting on time.
- Use laptop in class only for learning purposes.
- Promptly access the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information.
- Disclose any use of AI tools as required by each assignment, and be able to explain and defend all submitted work.

- Python 3.10+ with Google Colab or Jupyter Notebook
- A code/text editor (e.g., VS Code)
- A model API endpoint provided by the instructor for Lab 3 (mock available offline)

clos.CLO Details: Describe how generative AI models work at an intuitive, non-mathematical level.
Apply prompt engineering techniques to obtain useful, reliable outputs from generative models.

Build a small generative AI application end to end, retrieval-augmented generation, structured output validation, basic agent/tool use, and an appropriate customization strategy (prompting, RAG, or fine-tuning).
Evaluate generative AI outputs and systems using rubrics, test sets, model-as-judge methods, and analysis of failure modes.
Analyze the ethical, social, legal, and governance implications of generative AI and apply responsible-use practices.

metadata.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 121h online + 3h offline + 1h TE + 2h PE + 23h self-study
metadata.Description: Advanced Generative AI (AGA) studies how modern large language models (LLMs) and the generative-AI stack are built, adapted, evaluated, and deployed. This technology is one of the most rapidly evolving areas of machine learning, and demand is growing for professionals able to construct, fine-tune, align, and ship production-quality LLM-based systems. The course covers transformer architectures and data preparation, foundational and transformer-based language modelling, parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA, QLoRA), advanced alignment (RLHF, PPO, DPO), and the design of LLM-powered applications using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), LangChain, and AI agents. By the end of this specialization, students will be ready to design generative-AI applications that perform text generation, classification, translation, retrieval-augmented question answering, and build LLM-powered agents.
metadata.StudentTasks: Student must get the certification of Generative AI Engineering with LLMs Specialization from Coursera to be accepted to the final examination
metadata.Note: 1. Complete the online course to be allowed to take Final Exam 2. Final Exam is included of Final Theory Exam (TE) & Final Practical Exam (PE): 100% 3. Students who complete all MOOCs before the course deadline will receive 1 bonus point; otherwise, no bonus point will be awarded. 4. Completion Criteria: Final TE Score >=4 & Final PE Score >=4 & FR >= 5 (FR = min(10, (Final TE Score + Final PE Score)/2 + bonus)

metadata.Description: Multimodal AI course aim on building AI systems that operate across modalities - vision, language, audio, video, 3D, and embodiment. The course frames multimodality through four core problems (representation, alignment, fusion, translation) and proceeds through cross-modal representations (CLIP, SigLIP, ImageBind), fusion architectures (cross-attention, Perceiver, Q-Former, gated cross-attention), vision-language and unified models (LLaVA, BLIP-2, Flamingo, Chameleon/Janus families), speech and audio, video and world models, 3D and embodied agents, multimodal reasoning / agents / RAG, evaluation (benchmark saturation, hallucination), efficiency and deployment, and safety/provenance/frontiers. Mathematical depth is assumed from the prerequisites (Deep Learning, Advanced Generative AI); this course focuses on architectures, training recipes, evaluation, and hands-on multimodal systems.

clos.CLO Details: Identify and characterize multimodal AI systems and the four core problems of multimodal machine learning - representation, alignment, fusion, and translation.
Build cross-modal representations using contrastive and self-supervised methods, and evaluate them via zero-shot transfer and cross-modal retrieval.
Design and implement fusion architectures (cross-attention, latent bottlenecks, connector modules) that combine heterogeneous modalities.
Apply vision-language and unified multimodal architectures (LLaVA, BLIP-2, Flamingo, and unified token/diffusion-transformer families) and instruction-tune them.
Apply multimodal techniques to non-image modalities - speech, audio, video, 3D, and embodied agents - and to cross-modal generation.
Engineer multimodal reasoning, agent, and retrieval systems, and address the input-size and latency challenges of deploying them.
Evaluate multimodal systems with appropriate benchmarks and protocols, recognizing saturation and the migrating frontier, and run hallucination and grounding diagnostics.
Analyze the safety, provenance, bias, and privacy issues specific to multimodal AI - deepfakes, watermarking, and biometric data.

metadata.Syllabus Name: GenAI Project_Dự án TTNT tạo sinh
metadata.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
metadata.Description:
This capstone project course is designed to consolidate and apply students' knowledge in generative AI and large language models through a substantial team project. Students scope, design, build, evaluate, and present a non-trivial generative AI system or empirical study. Topics applied include:
- The application of generative AI techniques (LLMs, diffusion, RAG, agents, fine-tuning) to solve practical problems.
- The identification and adaptation of generative AI methodologies from current research for specific use cases.
- The development of a comprehensive solution approach using prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, fine-tuning (LoRA / QLoRA), or agent design.
- The evaluation and analysis of generative outputs using appropriate metrics (perplexity, ROUGE, faithfulness, FID, human / LLM-as-judge protocols) and rigorous failure-mode analysis.
- Recognition of appropriate scenarios for prompting vs RAG vs fine-tuning vs agent design.
- Selection of suitable metrics and benchmarks for generative-system evaluation.
- Understanding the ethical, safety, provenance, and legal implications of generative AI (hallucination, bias, deepfakes, copyright, content provenance / C2PA).
- Implementation and reflection on generative pipelines including data preparation, model adaptation, inference / serving, and post-deployment monitoring.
- Effective teamwork and project management across a multi-phase delivery.
metadata.StudentTasks:
- Select a suitable generative AI project and form teams (2-3 members).
- Allocate and schedule tasks among team members.
- Develop a project output that meets the specified requirements and demonstrates individual contribution.
- Submit four progressive reports (Proposal; Data & Baseline; Model & Results; Final Project Report) on time per the schedule.
- Disclose any use of AI tools as required by each report, and be able to explain and defend all submitted work and code.
- Present and defend the project in front of a review panel at the final oral examination.
- Promptly access the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information.
metadata.Tools:
- Programming Languages: Python 3.10+
- Software Tools: Jupyter Notebook / Google Colab, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Diffusers, PEFT, TRL, LangChain, vLLM
- Models: Hosted frontier APIs (Claude, GPT, Gemini) and open-weight families (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek)
- Datasets: Hugging Face Datasets, Kaggle, publicly licensed corpora
- Additional Resources: Papers with Code, arXiv, GitHub, Hugging Face Hub, Weights & Biases for experiment tracking
metadata.Note:
- The essential capstone project is mandatory, focusing on solving a real-world generative-AI problem. It consists of four progressive reports and a final oral presentation.
- The final mark is determined by summing the weighted scores of: Report 1 - Project Proposal (10%), Report 2 - Data & Baseline (20%), Report 3 - Model & Results (30%), Report 4 - Final Project Report (10%), and Final Exam - Oral group presentation (30%).
- The final exam (oral group presentation) takes place in class, individually evaluated by one professor / lecturer or a review panel.
- Completion Criteria: every assessment component > 0 AND Final Exam Score >= 4 AND Final Result >= 5.

clos.CLO Details: Identify relevant generative-AI techniques (LLMs, diffusion, multimodal, RAG, agents, fine-tuning, alignment) for a capstone topic.
Formulate problem statements, scope, objectives, and success criteria in a project proposal.
Plan data preparation, model selection, and licensing/ethics review.
Conduct baseline analysis using pre-trained models, prompting, and in-context learning.
Develop and adapt generative-AI systems to project requirements.
Evaluate and optimize systems using appropriate metrics and protocols, with attention to contamination and saturation.
Interpret outputs and failure modes (hallucination, bias, jailbreak) and visualize results for stakeholders.
Summarize conclusions and actionable recommendations, including deployment and cost/latency trade-offs.
Compile a final report with an explicit ethics, safety, and provenance subsection.
Deliver oral presentations with live demonstrations and Q&A defense.
